release_notes: 911 Inspection Dimensions now fills in the weld prep angles too. It already read the bevel codes off the drawings, but the angle isn't printed there - it lives in the Electric Boat bevel book. All 947 bevel sheets have been transcribed and now ship with the app, so a code on a drawing becomes a real number on the inspection sheet. SB, FB and WB preps were being skipped entirely before and now work; a two-sided callout is recorded as two entries; a VOIDed code names its replacement instead of writing a value; and a prep whose sheet prints no angle lands in a "needs a decision" list instead of quietly writing nothing. Where the reader gets a code slightly wrong it repairs the clear-cut cases and, for the rest, names the closest valid code without ever guessing onto a form. Checked against 90 real packets. The Pallet Stamper now stamps the work packet, not the drawing binder - it was taking the first PDF in the order folder, which since binders arrived is usually a drawing, so the packet the floor reads stayed blank; stamps left on drawings are removed. Long folder paths no longer break file writes: the Windows 260-character limit was making apps fail with a misleading "file not found", and it's fixed across all 25 apps. FormingFinder tracks the same part built for two different orders instead of dropping the second. Kitting prints orders of more than ten parts in full. The 911 LST Organizer accepts the nesting software's new 1D diagram format, which had been failing every run. And the Assistant quick note no longer jumps the cursor to the top while you type. Apps that read from OneDrive now download files while you're still answering prompts, so the waiting overlaps with the work.
